teams.heading: Fiji Latui reduced to 12 men in 62-12 defeat to Ireland XV
teams.body: Fiji Latui, the Fijian development side, picked up four first-half yellow cards in Friday's 62-12 defeat to the Ireland XV at Virgin Media Park. Three came in five minutes and left them with 12 men for a spell. Isaia Lotawa's no-arms tackle conceded a penalty try, and Apisalome Kuruisaqila was binned for a deliberate knock-on. Mesake Doge, carded for a high tackle, received a 20-minute red for collapsing a third successive scrum 30 seconds after returning. Pita Lesivoukionoilau's seventh-minute interception try had given Fiji their only lead.

lead.why: The only NEW item (#1), foreign press reaction to the 21-16 win over Italy, retells a story already run on Sunday, so the unreported Fiji Latui match leads.

teams.heading: Borthwick hopeful over Tommy Freeman's quad niggle after 37-12 All Blacks win
teams.body: Tommy Freeman pulled out of the starting XV hours before Saturday's 37-12 win over New Zealand with a quad niggle and has no firm return date. Steve Borthwick said: “Maybe there’s a chance for next week, but it’s probably too early to say that right now.” Cadan Murley started in his place. Fin Smith, replaced after 55 minutes, had cramp in both legs, and Borthwick expects a quick recovery. Fans in the app took the result well: 39 answered, and 97% were buzzing.

lead.why: Fresh hard news on a key England winger's fitness before the New Zealand rematch, ahead of a pundit column.

teams.heading: Fabien Galthié recalls Thomas Ramos to France's 42 for Springboks final
teams.body: Ramos is back after several weeks sidelined by a thigh injury, and Rugbyrama reckons his return would push Théo Attissogbe to the wing for the Twickenham final against South Africa. Grégory Alldritt misses out with a physical complaint, replaced by La Rochelle clubmate Oscar Jegou. Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang, hurt in the 45-17 win over Argentina, is absent with an ankle problem. Jean-Baptiste Gros, a late withdrawal against the Pumas, stays in the group, and the staff hope he can make the final.

lead.why: A fresh senior-squad announcement for the final, with Ramos back, Alldritt out and Grandidier-Nkanang ruled out of the group.

teams.heading: Ireland to face ex-defence coach Les Kiss' Wallabies in fifth-place play-off
teams.body: Third place in the Northern Hemisphere ladder sends Andy Farrell's side to Twickenham for the Nations Championship fifth-place final, and the opponent is a familiar face. Kiss, the former Ireland defence coach and Ulster boss, succeeded Joe Schmidt as Wallabies head coach earlier this year, and his side sealed third in the Southern Hemisphere table by beating Wales 29-26 on Saturday. All six play-off games are there next weekend, with France meeting South Africa — beaten in Dublin — in the final.

lead.why: Fresh, two-outlet news confirming Ireland's next opponent, with an ex-Ireland coach in the other dugout.

teams.heading: Italy slip to 12th in world rankings after 16-21 Fiji defeat
teams.body: Saturday's defeat in Udine cost Quesada's side 0.80 rating points, and the slide to 75.03 let Japan through into 11th. Japan's own loss to Scotland left their total untouched. The bigger worry sits below: Georgia beat the United States and are only 0.17 points behind on 74.86. Fiji gained the same 0.80 and now trail Wales in ninth by 0.07. It caps a group stage of six defeats in six before finals weekend at Twickenham.

lead.why: It is the only new event about Italy: a world ranking drop that followed the Fiji result, with Georgia now close behind.

teams.heading: Matt Fagerson injured in 67-5 Japan rout as Scotland turn to Argentina
teams.body: Scotland's 67-5 win over Japan at Murrayfield on Saturday left a fitness worry before the Nations Championship finale against Argentina at Twickenham. "Matt Fagerson went through a lot of work and hopefully his injury isn't serious," said Gregor Townsend, who also hailed Ollie Leatherbarrow's work on both sides of the ball. Today's press carries no detail on the extent of it. Stand-in captain Stafford McDowall, deputising for Sione Tuipulotu and Rory Darge, said the side kept their foot on the throat in the second half.

lead.why: Only new item; it carries hard news on Matt Fagerson's injury before the Argentina finale.

teams.heading: Tandy vows Wales rotation for Japan after 26-29 loss and Williams injury
teams.body: Wales meet Eddie Jones' Japan for ninth place at Twickenham, a fifth meeting in 16 months, and Tandy insisted: "It doesn’t matter who wears the shirt – we’ve got to perform." Scrum-half Tomos Williams went off early in the second half against Australia with a groin injury and will be assessed. Tandy praised low-cap replacements Kane James, Louie Hennessey and Reuben Morgan-Williams, who all got solid minutes off the bench. Japan have conceded 145 points to England and Scotland over the last two weeks.

lead.why: It is new hard news about Wales's next test: Tandy has promised rotation and Tomos Williams has an injury.

teams.heading: Mayco Vivas red card and early injuries sink Pumas 45-17 in Paris
teams.body: Saturday's 45-17 defeat in Paris began unravelling before kick-off, when Santiago Chocobares withdrew and Justo Piccardo moved to inside centre. Bautista Delguy and Boris Wenger then went off early and never returned. Piccardo's try and Tomás Albornoz's boot still had Argentina 10-7 up before France led 14-10 at the break. Hollie Davidson's yellow for Vivas became red, Julián Montoya was also carded, and France pulled clear with three tries in quick succession. Scotland await in the battle for seventh.

lead.why: The match report carries the red card and injury fallout from Argentina's defeat, which yesterday's anthem story did not cover.

teams.heading: Les Kiss' Wallabies book Ireland fifth-place play-off with 29-26 Wales win
teams.body: Saturday's 29-26 victory in Cardiff sealed third place in the Southern Hemisphere table, which pairs Australia with Andy Farrell's Ireland, third in the Northern Hemisphere ladder, at Twickenham. It is a reunion of sorts for Kiss, the former Ireland defence coach and Ulster boss who succeeded Joe Schmidt earlier this year. The win also ended a four-match losing streak, and captain Harry Wilson wants more: "We want to go out there next week, get a victory next week and we want to have a big leap going into 2027."

lead.why: A fresh, two-outlet event that sets Australia's next opponent, distinct from yesterday's match-result lead.

teams.heading: Japan to face Wales in London after 67-5 Murrayfield loss to Scotland
teams.body: Kyodo reports that Saturday's 67-5 defeat at Murrayfield left Eddie Jones' side fifth in the six-team Southern Hemisphere group. That sets up a meeting on the finals weekend in London with Wales, the Northern Hemisphere's fifth-placed team. Only Takuro Matsunaga's 52nd-minute try spared Japan a nil after they trailed 29-0 at half-time, a week on from a 78-15 beating by England. South Africa and France contest the overall title the following day.

lead.why: The defeat and sin-bins have already run, so the new angle is where the result leaves Japan: a fifth-place meeting with Wales on finals weekend.

teams.heading: All Blacks fall to fifth in world rankings after 37-12 England defeat
teams.body: The slide cost New Zealand three places and 2.05 points, leaving them on 88.60 — behind England, who climbed to fourth on 89.04, and an Ireland side who leapt to second after beating South Africa, still top on 90.25. Less than a point and a half separates the top five. The All Blacks get an immediate rematch with England at Twickenham in the Nations Championship's third-place final, with Dave Rennie having conceded after the loss: "I'm a big part of that."

lead.why: The rankings drop is a fresh, concrete consequence of the England loss rather than another retelling of the match or more reaction to it.

teams.heading: Grant Williams targets discipline fix as Boks reach final despite 20-17 defeat
teams.body: Saturday's 20-17 loss to Ireland still sent South Africa into the Nations Championship final at Twickenham. France await again, after beating the Boks 21-19 in Paris and routing Argentina 45-17. Grant Williams, the scrumhalf-cum-wing, pinned the Dublin defeat on discipline: "They got into our half with stupid penalties and they converted." He wants everyone, one to 23, to take a hard look at themselves, and noted this group has never won a Nations Championship.

lead.why: The Boks booked a final rematch with France, and a player named the fix on the record.
